history.what: Harmonised: grid water measured at the meter (plant ÷ 0.92), state factors, all-in tariffs, ₹90 per US$, India capacity 1,789 MW.
Cooling table corrected from the October 2026 research; cooling-tower WUE 1.8 L/kWh in Bengaluru; reference PUEs aligned across tools.
One standards module for every model; ranges, owners and review dates for each value; capex stacks, Scope 3, embodied carbon, shadow prices and climate horizons added.

Workload utilisation added (training 0.90, inference 0.70, general-purpose 0.65) and a 2% fixed electrical overhead; the designer now splits energy, water and carbon by workload and weights PUE and WUE by energy.

Audit: CEA v22.0 grid factor 0.675 t/MWh (FY2025-26) with operating, build and combined margins; coal plant water 3.5 m³/MWh from MoEFCC limits and measured averages (was 5.55), so India grid water at the meter is 2.9 L/kWh (was 4.5); carbon and water both use the national grid by default (CEA publishes no state factors), state generation mixes kept as a sensitivity; reservoir hydro 10 L/kWh everywhere; one reference AI campus (40% training, utilisation 0.78) and conventional hall (0.65); India demand from the CEA midterm review; measured energy per prompt.

AI accelerators added: one sourced record for each of nine chips (specifications, server power per GPU, MLPerf Inference Server throughput per GPU, rental prices), read by the cluster sizer, the design check, the data centre model and the GPU-hour calculator. Review every six months: software alone moved MLPerf results by up to 38% between rounds.
